_comment: Golden record for scripts/12_xpurt_coloc_sweep.sh -- the co-located schedule for two networks on the dual-hart Rocket, with SignDetLite PERIODIC at T = 1000 ms (1.00 fps, 4 declared instances) and Moonshine the NON-PERIODIC job the makespan measures. 9 heuristic policies + 2 CP-SAT paths x {none, dram} contention x {plain, compact} = 44 cells. Host only: no board, no bitstream. Every DURATION in it was measured on one -- Moonshine's per dispatch on 0x5A5A0035 and SignDetLite's on 0x5A5A0038, both at 40.000 MHz -- and the PLACEMENT is the solver's.
_the_result: AT T = 1000 ms, UNDER MEASURED DRAM CONTENTION, COMPACTION IS WHAT CROSSES THE WINDOW. `--scheduler cpsat` lands Moonshine at 5,412.25 ms with the contention model installed; with XPURT_COMPACT=1 the same solve lands at 3,992.30 ms. 1,419.95 ms recovered, op_deadline_miss_count 0 in BOTH -- so no detector frame was traded for it. On the uncontended arm the same pass is worth 376.15 ms (3,649.06 -> 3,272.91). AND NONE OF THE NINE HEURISTICS CLEARS BOTH OBJECTIVES AT ALL: all 36 heuristic cells fail the real-time test. The best makespan (heft = critical_path, 4,251.12 ms) misses three of the four detector windows; edf, the only policy that lands all four, ends 6,076.00 ms -- 2,076 ms past the reference. QUOTE THE THREE CROSSINGS TOGETHER: 0.25 fps heuristic, 1.0 fps achieved, 2.62 fps capacity. The middle figure is a solver result, not the machine's limit.
_4000ms_is_a_reference_not_a_constraint: Moonshine carries no period and no window_duration in this spec, so nothing the solver saw made 4,000 ms a deadline. It is the real-time-factor-1 utterance window, compared against after the fact. THE FOUR DETECTOR WINDOWS ARE the constraints. `op_deadline_miss_count` counts late DETECTOR dispatches only.
_real_time_ok_is_derived_here: The string `real_time_ok` occurs nowhere in the XPU-RT checkout: no solver computes it and no schedule, metrics or report file carries it. It is a two-part test applied by scripts/lib/b157_report.py -- Moonshine's end inside the 4,000 ms reference AND every detector instance inside its own window. A reader who takes it for solver output will believe 4,000 ms was enforced, and it never was. Each row's `real_time_ok` below is that derivation, not a measurement.

_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself._comment: Four checks decide whether a row may be believed at all, and each of them exists because the corresponding mistake was made and was invisible in the makespan column.
_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself.contention_arm_re_derived_from_each_log: The spec's `"contention": {"enabled": true, "path": ...}` block IS NEVER READ. The string `contention` does not occur in run_xpurt_schedule.py's spec parsing; only `--contention PATH` installs a model. It is possible to solve the `none` arm for hours and file the result as `dram`. So every cell's arm is re-derived from its OWN log -- `none` must carry no '--contention: loaded' line, `dram` must name contention_b4_dram.json -- and a cell whose log disagrees with its directory is marked unverified rather than reported. Reference: 44 of 44 agree, and dram/plain reproduces the archived 5412.249935046185 exactly.
_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself.compaction_arm_read_back_from_the_artifa: XPURT_COMPACT lands in metadata.solve_env.env of every emitted schedule, so the arm is read out of what the solver wrote rather than assumed from the launcher. Reference: 44 of 44.
_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself.no_machine_overlap: Two dispatches on one machine may not overlap, measured with the durations the schedule itself emits. This matters most on `dram`, where greedy scales durations at lookup time but the CP-SAT model and the compaction pass read raw durations -- a plan made on solo costs and emitted with scaled ones could collide. Reference: 0 overlaps in all 44.
_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself.hard_machine_exclusion: Every dispatch must land on a machine its dispatch graph's `infeasible_machines` does not forbid. A non-empty violation list invalidates every makespan in that file. Reference: 0 in all 40 valid cells, 74 in the 4 refused ones.
_what_the_sweep_must_prove_about_itself.ortools_actually_present: cpsat_available() tries $XPURT_CPSAT_PYTHON and then the PATH's python3 -- never sys.executable -- so a venv interpreter named by absolute path without the env var silently falls back to a python3 with no ortools. Every log is grepped for a surviving 'no interpreter with ortools'. Reference: 0.

headline_cells._comment: The rows worth quoting, read out of the table below.

cpsat_none_compact._note: The shortest Moonshine end in all 44 cells, and it is VALID.

cpsat_dram_compact._note: 1,419.95 ms recovered against dram/plain, op_deadline_miss_count 0 in both.

_refused_cells: FOUR CELLS ARE REFUSED, NOT REPORTED. The `cpsat_warmbest_b157` path -- the one that genuinely keeps a warm start, 2,285 of 2,285 operations hinted against 19.4 % of non-fixed variables on `--scheduler cpsat` -- placed dispatches on machines their own dispatch graph forbids. 74 violations across the four cells. moonshine_dispatch_1538 (linear_s8, infeasible_machines ['CPU_P#0']) was placed ON CPU_P#0, and moonshine_dispatch_1727 (permute4_s8, infeasible_machines ['CPU_E#0']) ON CPU_E#0. CPU_P is hart 0, which has the MBP P-extension and no engine; CPU_E is hart 1, which has the RoccMoon engine and no P-extension. Each of those is an ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION on silicon. CAUSE: cpsat_scheduler.cpsat_schedule builds its model from DecoderContext, and schedule_decoder.py contains the string `infeasible` ZERO times. The exclusion is a SET on the Operation, not an infinite cost, and build_payload excludes a combination only when its duration is non-finite -- so the forbidden cells arrive as cheap legal options and the emitted durations look ordinary (114.25 ms). Nothing in the artifact reads as wrong. `--scheduler cpsat` and the nine heuristics build feasible combinations explicitly and have 0 violations in all 40 other cells.
_and_the_lesson_is_not_the_one_it_looks_: It is tempting to read the refusal as having rescued the lab from a tempting answer. It did not: THE INVALID CELLS WERE MOSTLY SLOWER AS WELL AS ILLEGAL, so refusing them cost nothing. Warmbest is shorter in ONE of the four pairs (dram/plain, 5,182.71 against 5,412.25); the registry path wins the other three, and the shortest Moonshine end in all 44 cells -- 3,272.91 ms -- is a VALID one. There is no speed-for-validity trade here to go looking for. The real lesson is the opposite: INVALIDITY IS INVISIBLE IN THE MAKESPAN COLUMN IN EITHER DIRECTION. A schedule that breaks the machine model can be faster or slower than a legal one, and the number alone never says which -- which is exactly why the audit has to GATE the result rather than annotate it. On counting: 74 violations is right. The four cells' per-cell distinct dispatch counts sum to 37 (10+9+13+5), which is 37 (cell, dispatch) pairs; the number of DISTINCT DISPATCH NAMES across the four is 32. Either figure is defensible if it is named.
_compaction_on_the_heuristics: A bit-exact no-op, as predicted, and that is the point of running it: 0.000 ms recovered and 0 of 2,285 dispatches moved in all 18 plain-vs-compact heuristic pairs. A list scheduler already places every op at its earliest feasible instant, so there is nothing to left-shift. The pass only pays where a solver leaves joint idle. NOTE THE TWO THINGS THAT MAKE COMPACTION REACHABLE AT ALL: XPURT_COMPACT is applied only by schedulers.get_scheduler(), so it is a silent no-op on any bare `--solver <non-milp>` path while metadata.solve_env.env still records it as set; and _wrap_with_compaction discards its own result for a scheduler that returns a 2-tuple where the registry contract is 4.
_how_to_tell_a_live_solve_from_a_dead_on: A long CP-SAT cell writes a 0-BYTE LOG AND NO METRICS JSON UNTIL IT EXITS: Python block-buffers stdout to a file, and run_xpurt_schedule.py writes the schedule only after the solver returns. Checking for output files reports a healthy solve as dead. Liveness is `ps -eo pid,etime,time` -- elapsed AND CPU time, since 8 workers x 46 min is ~6.1 CPU-hours for one warm-start cell -- plus /proc/<pid>/fd/1 showing the open write handle on the log. `ps -C python3` matches nothing if your venv's binary is named `python`.
_reproducibility: CP-SAT is deterministic ONLY at XPURT_CPSAT_WORKERS=1. The `--scheduler cpsat` cells here were solved at 1 worker and reproduce bit-exactly: nonperiodic_makespan_ms 3649.05855611 on two independent runs, delta 0.0, ALL 2,285 DISPATCHES IDENTICAL IN START TIME AND TARGET -- only wall time differed (2,723.98 s against 2,753.11 s), which is machine load. Above one worker the answer depends on how much search the wall budget bought and on thread interleaving, so the 8-worker cells are NOT reproducible to the millisecond. The worker count is recorded in metadata.solve_env of every schedule rather than assumed. One worker is also not a neutral default: on an adjacent cell at a 300 s budget, 1 worker gave 4,031.77 ms with 16 deadline misses where 8 gave 3,133.40 ms with none.
_caveats: PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED. The durations are board-measured; the placement is the solver's, and the runtime does not execute this plan. Two-hart overlap has been demonstrated on silicon at ONE interleave point and nothing wider.
The reference sweep ran on a loaded machine (load average 40-78 on 48 cores). CP-SAT's answer at a fixed WALL budget depends on how much search that budget buys.
4,000 ms is a reference, never a constraint. The four detector windows are the constraints.
_artifacts_not_committed: The sweep writes 44 logs, 132 schedule/metrics/report JSONs and 44 per-cell renders -- about 85 MB of schedules alone. None of it is in this repository: it is what your run produces, under out/b157/. What IS here is everything the solve READS (fpga/pynq-z2/xpurt/), the tooling, and this table to check the answer against.
